text.en: We use a water pot, a gullak, a bird bath and a kulhad cup. What are they made of, and who makes them and how? Today we follow a potter's family and a boy who loves to watch walls grow.

In a town by the sea, Mini watched her Appooppan, her grandfather, make a pot. He took clay and made it wet, adding enough water to get the right thickness. He pounded the clay well and kneaded it like dough, so that it was neither too watery nor too dry. Then he put the clay on a stone wheel and shaped it by spinning the wheel. When the pots had dried, Ammu moved them into a very hot oven called a kiln, where the fire baked them. Then the pot was ready for use, and the family made patterns on some pots to make them look more beautiful.
Baking in the kiln makes the soft clay hard and strong, so the pot does not melt in water. Potters make water pots, cups like kulhads, piggy banks called gullaks, bird baths and many other things. Mini was too young to use the wheel, but she helped by making patterns and colouring the pots. Her favourite clay item was her piggy bank, which she decorated and used to save money. We can help our parents and grandparents in small ways too.
With the help of elders we can make our own clay. We collect soil from a wet or muddy place and remove big pebbles, sand, leaves and plant parts using a net or sieve. We put the soil in a flat vessel of water, and after a few days we pour away the water on top. Then we make a dough that we can shape into a ball, and make two things we like and dry them in the sun.
Patterns are found everywhere in nature, like spots on a leopard and stripes on a squirrel. Neem leaves on a branch make a pattern, and so do the skins of zebras, peacocks, cats, tigers, butterflies and fish. Artists who paint on pots get ideas from nature, using its shapes and colours. A pattern has repeating shapes and lines, and we can find patterns on plants, animals and things, and decorate objects with our own patterns. Pottery from different parts of India has beautiful patterns.
Bricks are also made of mud, just like the pots Appooppan made. Bricks are shaped in moulds, like the moulds for idli, cake, dhokla or kulfi, and become hard after baking in a kiln. Bricks are used to build houses, schools and hospitals. Rohan lives in Jaipur and loves to watch brick walls grow day by day until they become a big building.
Not all houses are made of bricks. In warm areas people build traditional mud houses with natural materials like grass and wood to keep inside cool. Instead of cement, many use cow dung to make smooth walls and floors, which keeps the heat out and insects away. Mud houses are better for the environment because they use natural materials found nearby. We can look at the houses around us and find out what they are made of.
We can make small bricks from a matchbox mould, paper boxes, clay or atta dough and stack them in two ways to see which wall is sturdier. Rohan's father follows safety rules at work: he wears a helmet with a strap, a safety vest and sturdy shoes. We also have safety rules at home and at school.

problem.en: Put the steps of pot making in order.

text.en: Wet the clay and add enough water.

why.en: The clay should be neither too watery nor too dry.

text.en: Pound and knead it like dough.
Shape it on the spinning stone wheel.

why.en: The wheel gives the round shape.

text.en: Let it dry, then bake in the kiln.
Make patterns to decorate it.

problem.en: Which is sturdier: bricks stacked in a staggered pattern or in straight columns?

text.en: Stack small bricks both ways with some clay or atta.
Push gently on each wall.

why.en: The one that stays up longer is sturdier.

text.en: The staggered wall holds better because each brick sits across the gap below.

problem.en: Why do some people build mud houses in warm areas?

text.en: Mud, grass and wood are natural materials.

why.en: They are easy to find nearby.

text.en: Cow dung on walls and floors keeps heat out.
It also keeps insects away.

why.en: So the house is comfortable and good for the environment.

prompt.en: Tell a friend how a pot is made and why a kiln is needed.

requiredIdeas.en: The clay is wetted, pounded and kneaded, then shaped on a wheel
The pot is dried and baked in a kiln so that it becomes hard
Patterns come from ideas in nature
Bricks are also made of mud and baked in a kiln

commonMisconceptions.en: A pot is ready as soon as it is shaped
All houses are made of bricks

points.en: A potter wets, pounds and kneads clay, shapes it on a wheel, dries it and bakes it in a kiln.
A kiln is a very hot oven that makes clay pots and bricks hard.
Patterns have repeating shapes and lines and are found in plants, animals and things.
Bricks are made in moulds from mud and baked, and houses can also be made of mud, grass and wood.
Safety rules, like wearing a helmet at a building site, keep us safe.
